newsitem.title: USA: US Spot Products-Gasolines firm, helped by NYMEX.
newsitem.headline: US Spot Products-Gasolines firm, helped by NYMEX.

text.p: U.S. gasoline prices jumped higher during early Wednesday action, boosted by a rebound on the NYMEX as well as strength in the Gulf Coast and Midcontinent differentials.
However, New York Harbor regular gasoline differentials remained fairly weak on ample supplies, traders said.
On the NYMEX, July gasoline rallied 1.10 cents to 57.50 cents a gallon, pulling along the July heating oil, which gained 0.65 cent to sit at 52.30 cents a gallon.
U.S. GULF
Gasoline differentials popped up as buyers chased prompt barrels higher, especially in the premium grades, traders said.
"The high octanes are pretty tight at this point," one Gulf player said.
Prompt premium conventional V1 gasoline was talked at about 5.50 cents over the regular conventional M1 gasoline, a gain of about 0.25 cent from late Tuesday.
"We've had several people looking for the V1 over the past few days," the trader said.
Premium reformulated D1 gasoline also attracted buying interest, with prompt barrels seen at 6.50 to 6.75 cents over the conventional M1, or about 5.50 cents over the July NYMEX.
Market watchers said there appeared to be no new refinery problems on the Gulf Coast, though Citgo has been a buyer in the premium grades following the fire at its alkylation unit on May 12.

Prompt M1 barrels changed hands at 1.25 cents under the July NYMEX, a gain of about 0.25 cent on the day as refiners moved to cover commitments ahead of the scheduling deadline today on the Colonial Pipeline.
MIDCONTINENT

Group Three unleaded gasoline differentials remained firm on Wednesday amid short covering due to continued delays along the Explorer Pipeline. The pipeline confirmed market talk that the 17th cycle will be delayed about nine days, arriving into Tulsa, Oklahoma about July 1 instead of June 22.
"Players who shorted the any month are now trying to cover themselves," said a gasoline trader.

The pipeline, however, has been behind schedule for the past month since maintenance earlier this spring set operations back. Pipeline officials said they were surprised the delay caused market reaction.
"We send a schedule update every three days. Most people should have known about the delay," said a pipeline scheduler.
Prompt Group Three unleaded differentials were done at 6.25 cents over the July NYMEX, a quarter cent off from Tuesday afternoon but still above late Monday. Any month barrels traded at 3.50 cents.
Strong interest in Chicago markets also gave a half cent boost to unleaded gasoline differentials to 4.00 to 4.50 cents over the July NYMEX print.
NEW YORK HARBOR
Thinly traded premium conventional unleaded gasoline attracted several players Wednesday in the Harbor, pushing up differentials, while reformulated gasoline clung to lower levels.

"We have got a couple of bidders for V2 (premium conventional unleaded) and that is causing the pop. With the reformulated, there are still more sellers than buyers when there is a lot of supply," said a Harbor dealer.
Premium conventional unleaded was offered at 4.50 cents over NYMEX July gasoline versus 4.00 cents Tuesday. Reformulated was bid at 0.25 cent under and offered even with July gasoline.
"I think 0.10 cent under the screen is where it can get done," said a trader of reformulated gasoline.

Heating oil differentials were softer, with Sun Co posting its offer at 0.40 cent under versus the market's offer of 0.10 cent under Tuesday. Tuesday evening, the American Petroleum Institute (API) said that for the week ended June, heating oil stocks rose 1.5 million barrels in the U.S. Northeast.
The API said gasoline rose 433,000 barrels in the region softening conventional unleaded gasoline differentials with the bid around 2.60 cents under July gasoline versus 2.50 under Tuesday.
-- New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1620
